answer: Counting every wall section built by every dynasty, the Great Wall is about 21,196 km (roughly 13,171 miles) long. China's cultural heritage administration announced that figure in June 2012, after a survey that started in 2007 [1][2]. You'll often see a shorter number, about 8,850 km (5,500 miles). That covers only the Ming dynasty wall, built 1368–1644, which includes most of the best-preserved sections that visitors see today [2][3]. It was also the preliminary result released in 2009 [1]. Both lengths add up many separate walls, trenches and natural barriers, so the wall isn't one continuous line [1][3].
